content.text:
I made four small improvements to `0.html`, but none of them are tested: my attempt to render the page in headless Chrome was blocked by this session's permissions. The file was already in good shape, so I kept the changes targeted rather than restructuring it.

## What changed

- **Stale colour after back/forward navigation**: a page restored from the browser's back/forward cache now re-reads the saved colour. Before, it could show an old colour if another tab had changed it in the meantime.
- **Hint line wrapping**: the hint text now uses `text-wrap: balance`, so on narrow windows it breaks into even lines instead of leaving one or two words on their own.
- **No-JavaScript message**: added a `<noscript>` note saying JavaScript is required to change the colour, since the button does nothing without it.
- **Tidier script**: loading the saved colour at startup and reacting to changes from other tabs now go through one `syncFromStorage()` function. I also moved `syncKeyHint()` up beside the other function declarations.

## Behaviour I left alone

- **Double-click reset conflicts with fast clicking**: every second click of a rapid sequence is ignored and the double-click resets to blue, so someone clicking quickly to cycle gets bounced back. A double-click also briefly shows the next colour before resetting. Fixing either means delaying single clicks or moving reset to a different gesture.
- **Forced-colours mode**: the circle takes the system button colour, so every colour looks the same and only the text label tells them apart. Adding `forced-color-adjust: none` would keep the colours but override the user's preference.
